page: Microsoft Azure D2nls_v6 is a network-optimized, low-memory virtual machine belonging to the Dnlv6 server family. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture. This configuration provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor features a cache hierarchy consisting of a 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, Intel AMX for deep learning, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

The server is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU density of 2.0 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable, requiring external network-attached storage for persistent data. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included with this virtual machine.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate a clear performance asymmetry. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the average range. However, multi-core and memory-bound metrics are constrained. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU physics test, and PassMark database operations all fall into the bottom 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large-block read and write speeds registering at 15.54 GB/sec and 11.76 GB/sec respectively. Redis SET operations achieve 2.28 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaches 3.59 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2nls_v6 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring dedicated high-frequency CPU execution but minimal memory overhead. The low memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core represents a significant tradeoff, making this server unsuitable for memory-intensive databases or complex multi-threaded processing. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic network-optimized routing, simple web serving, or small-scale utility workloads that can operate within a 4.0 GB memory footprint.
